files..github/workflows/ci.yml:
name: ci

on:
  pull_request:

permissions: {}

concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

# Steps for a feature you have not added (lint, tests, runtime config, Playwright) are skipped
# by their `if`, so this file stays the same as the project grows.
jobs:
  check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@ea17c68df8912ef543352723c149a84f56e3d413 # v6.1.0
      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version: lts/*
          cache: pnpm
      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
      - name: Lint
        if: hashFiles('.oxlintrc.json') != ''
        run: pnpm lint
      - name: Check formatting
        if: hashFiles('.prettierrc.json') != ''
        run: pnpm format:check
      - run: pnpm typecheck
      - run: pnpm run --if-present typecheck:tooling
      - name: Test
        run: pnpm run --if-present test
      - run: pnpm build
      - name: mfeflow doctor
        run: pnpm exec mfeflow doctor
      - name: mfeflow validate
        run: pnpm exec mfeflow validate
      - name: mfeflow check-compat
        run: pnpm exec mfeflow check-compat
      - name: mfeflow budget
        run: pnpm exec mfeflow budget
      - name: Check runtime config
        run: pnpm run --if-present check:runtime-config
      - name: Install Playwright browser
        if: hashFiles('playwright.config.ts') != ''
        run: pnpm exec playwright install --with-deps chromium
      - name: Playwright smoke test
        if: hashFiles('playwright.config.ts') != ''
        run: pnpm run test:e2e
      - name: Upload Playwright report
        if: failure() && hashFiles('playwright.config.ts') != ''
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: playwright-report
          path: node_modules/.cache/playwright/report
          retention-days: 7
files.AGENTS.md:
# AGENTS.md

Guidance for coding agents working in this repo.

- Package manager: pnpm (via corepack). Never npm or yarn. Versions live in the `catalog` of
  `pnpm-workspace.yaml`; add dependencies there and reference them as `catalog:`.
- `pnpm dev` runs the shell and every remote. `pnpm build` builds all of them. `mfeflow dev` does the same with
  per-app logs and picks up new remotes without a restart.
- Before finishing: `mfeflow doctor` (and `mfeflow validate`, `mfeflow check-compat`, `mfeflow budget` after a build) must exit 0.
- TypeScript 7, strict. Relative imports have no file extension (`./plan`, not `./plan.js`).
- Each remote is deployed on its own. A remote must not import from another remote or from
  the shell; talk through the registry, events or URLs.
- A remote's public surface is `src/exposed/`. Everything else is private to it.
- Add apps and features with the `mfeflow` CLI (`mfeflow add remote <name>`, `mfeflow features`).
  `mfeflow.json` is the CLI's record of the project; do not edit the file hashes by hand.
- Shared singletons (react, react-dom, `@mfeflow/runtime`) are provided by the shell. Do not
  bundle your own copy.
files.README.md:
# shopco-platform

A React micro-frontend platform made with [mfeflow](https://github.com/mfeflow/mfeflow):
one shell and independently deployable remotes, loaded at runtime through Module Federation.

```
apps/shell      the host: routes, layout, registry loading
apps/<remote>   one micro-frontend each, exposing ./App
registry/envs   which build of each remote every environment serves
mfeflow.json    what the CLI generated; `mfeflow add` reads and updates it
```

## Run it

```sh
pnpm install
pnpm dev
```

`pnpm dev` starts the shell on http://localhost:4300 and every remote on its own port
(see `registry/envs/dev`). The shell reads that dev registry and renders the remotes.

`mfeflow dev` does the same with a prefixed, coloured log per app, and it follows the project:
add a remote with `mfeflow add remote checkout` and it starts, and the shell lists it, without a restart.
Use a remote you already run elsewhere with `mfeflow dev --remote checkout=http://localhost:3001`,
or run a few apps with `--only shell,catalog`. Ctrl+C stops everything.

## Change it

```sh
mfeflow add remote checkout     # a new remote, its registry files and its shell route
mfeflow add <feature>           # see `mfeflow features`
```

## Check it

```sh
mfeflow doctor              # singletons, compatibility, config, drift; --fix repairs the safe ones
mfeflow validate            # mfeflow.json, every mfe.json and every registry entry
mfeflow check-compat        # each remote's shared ranges against its shell
mfeflow budget              # after `pnpm build`: first-load JS per shell and remote
```

All of them take `--json` and exit non-zero on errors, so they can run in CI. `mfeflow budget` checks each remote's entry
against the 10 KB a remote may add; set `budget.baselineKb` in `mfeflow.json` (your pages built as one app) to check
the shell against baseline + 32 KB too.

## Before you deploy

`registry/envs/staging` and `registry/envs/prod` point at `example.com`. Replace the hosts
with where you serve each remote (the shell expects `/mfe/<name>/` on its own origin).
The shell loads the registry from `/registry/index.json`, so serve one per environment.

files.docs/ci.md:
# CI

`.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs on every pull request: lint, formatting, typecheck, tests, build, then
`mfeflow doctor`, `validate`, `check-compat` and `budget`, the runtime-config check and the Playwright smoke test.
A step for a feature the project does not have is skipped, so adding `testing` or `env-t3` later needs no edit to the
workflow. Every action is pinned to a commit SHA, the workflow starts from `permissions: {}`, and the job gets
`contents: read` only. Dependabot or Renovate can keep the pins current.

Make the `check` job a required status check on your default branch (Settings, Rules, Rulesets).

## Preview deploys (not generated yet)

mfeflow does not generate a deploy workflow in this release: pushing remotes to a registry comes with the registry
features. When you add a deploy job, keep to this shape.

- Run it on `pull_request` with `contents: read` and `id-token: write`, and no repository secrets.
- Upload the build of one remote to its own path, for example `preview/<remote>/<pr-number>/`, never to the
  path production reads.
- Comment the override link on the pull request. `?mfe-override=<remote>@<url of its mf-manifest.json>` on the
  staging shell loads that build instead of the registered one (the shell honours it outside production only).
- Pull requests from forks get no `id-token`, so they cannot deploy; build them without a preview.

## OIDC instead of stored cloud keys

Let the job ask GitHub for a short-lived token and exchange it for cloud credentials; no access key sits in the
repository settings.

```yaml
permissions:
  id-token: write
  contents: read
steps:
  - uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@<sha>
    with:
      role-to-assume: arn:aws:iam::<account>:role/<team>-deploy
      aws-region: eu-west-1
```

Give each team a role that can write only its own prefixes (`mfe/<remote>/*` and `preview/<remote>/*`), and restrict the
role's trust policy to this repository, the `pull_request` or `main` ref, and the workflow file. The same pattern
works with Google Cloud (`google-github-actions/auth`) and Azure (`azure/login`).

    "oxlint": "catalog:",

    "prettier": "catalog:",
    "turbo": "catalog:",
    "typescript": "catalog:",
    "vitest": "catalog:",
    "zod": "catalog:"
  },
  "scripts": {
    "dev": "turbo run dev",
    "build": "turbo run build",
    "typecheck": "turbo run typecheck",
    "lint": "oxlint --type-aware --deny-warnings",
    "format": "prettier --write .",
    "format:check": "prettier --check .",
    "check:runtime-config": "node --experimental-strip-types scripts/check-runtime-config.ts",
    "typecheck:tooling": "tsc --noEmit",
    "test": "vitest run",
    "test:e2e": "playwright test"
  }
}
